newsitem.title: USA: NYS Gov says safety issues govern any Thruway toll.
newsitem.headline: NYS Gov says safety issues govern any Thruway toll.

text.p: New York State Gov. George Pataki on Tuesday said that the Thruway Authority would have to show that any increase in the tolls paid by the motorists who drive on its roads was needed to protect their safety.

The chairman of the Thruway Authority, Howard Stenberg, in late September proposed spending $1.5 billion over six years to repair the state's roads, bridges and canals, but promised that raising tolls would be a "last resort."
Only one-third of the program's costs could be funded with existing resources, leaving the gap to be met with tolls and bonds, the chairman of the Authority said.
The governor's remarks echoed those made by the chairman, as both officials recalled the 1987 collapse of Schoharie Creek Bridge, which led to the loss of 10 lives.
Pataki told reporters in Albany that he did not want to see a toll increase, explaining his Administration was trying to lower the cost of living and doing business in the state.

"(But) if it happens out of necessity because of a need to keep bridges from collapsing then I think that the first priority has to be safety, but consistent with that we want to see the lowest possible tolls."
The governor added that he felt it was appropriate for the Assembly transportation committee to hold hearings on the issue, and its last one is scheduled for Oct 10.
